# Gibbs Cancellation Obstruction

This is a scientific research repository about exact Gibbs stationarity under strictly local autonomous quantum dynamics. Read the model before generalizing a claim.

## Learning route

The sole educational anchor is Rivas and Huelga, Open Quantum Systems: An Introduction, first edition 2012, using author preprint arXiv:1104.5242v2. The preprint and published book have different section numbering; use the bridge's verified mapping.

- [Learning entrypoint](learning/README.md)
- [Source-to-project bridge and worked example](learning/bridge.md)
- [Exactly 30 common understanding milestones](learning/milestones.md): M01–M12 background/preliminaries; M13–M30 narrative/innovation.

For the physical story, read the learning bridge and science/interpretation.md. For a proof review, read science/model.md, local-kernel.md and gibbs-certificate.md, then accuracy-relaxation.md and local-construction.md. For numerical constants, use science/quantitative-witness.md together with the exact/interval verification guide. These routes are explanations and understanding targets; they contain no personal learner assessments.

## Scope that must be preserved

Five qubits on an open chain. Coherent terms and individual Lindblad jumps are supported onsite or on an adjacent pair. Total stationarity permits cancellation between local terms; neither detailed balance nor frustration freeness is assumed. The generic exact-kernel result fixes inverse temperature before taking the generic Hamiltonian set. The matching accuracy-relaxation law is a target-dependent high-temperature asymptotic statement under a norm cap on the entire generator. The continuous numerical interval certifies the positive construction, not full evaluation rank at every real temperature. No arbitrary-chain-length theorem or useful finite-error converse constant is established.

The original theorems constrain local coherent terms as well as individual jumps. The separately labelled global-K comparison keeps strict local jumps, permits exact attractive Gibbs preparation for 0<=beta<=.01, and excludes genuine dissipative stationarity for every real beta>=2.4. The middle interval is unresolved. Credit the pure-target stationary bound to the pinned Dissipative-Locality-Accuracy converse and global coherent completion to spectral stabilizability. Pure Hamiltonian stationarity remains possible. Do not infer a continuous evaluation-rank result from the positive reservoir interval.
